**Front Desk / Guest Services & Spa Operations Associate**

**Piedmont Springs | Oakland, CA**  
**Part-Time | Evening Shifts: 4:00 PM–11:00 PM | Weekend Availability Required**

Piedmont Springs is looking for a friendly, dependable, energetic person to join our Guest Services team.

**First, an important note: this is not a sedentary receptionist position.**

Although every member of our Guest Services team works at the front desk, this is an **active, hands-on position**. Our staff rotate between front-desk responsibilities and helping operate the spa throughout the shift.

On any given evening, you may be checking in guests and answering phones one moment, then walking through the facility to reset spa rooms, handle towels and laundry, check restrooms and common areas, restock supplies, or assist with other operational needs the next.

**If you're looking for a job where you'll spend most of your shift sitting behind a desk, this probably isn't the right position for you.**

On the other hand, if you enjoy staying busy, moving around, helping customers, working independently, and having different things to do throughout your shift, you may be exactly who we're looking for.

**What You'll Do**

Our Guest Services staff are responsible for helping provide a welcoming experience for our customers while keeping the spa operating smoothly. Responsibilities include:

* Greeting customers and providing friendly, professional service

* Answering phones and booking appointments
* Learning our services and helping customers select and schedule them

jobs.title: Learning & Development Lead, Operations
jobs.description:
**Learning & Development Lead — Operations**

**Role Overview**

The Learning & Development Lead owns training and readiness for Physical Intelligence's robot operator workforce.

This person is responsible for designing and running the systems that take a new operator from candidate work trial through their first 30–60 days, with the goal of getting people productive quickly while maintaining a high quality bar.

They also own ongoing training as the work changes. When researchers introduce new robot workflows, tasks, tools, or operating procedures, the Learning & Development Lead translates those changes into training that can be rolled out quickly and consistently across the operation.

This is a highly operational training role. We are looking for someone who has built or owned training programs for hourly or frontline employees and knows how to turn complex work into a simple, repeatable learning process.

**Responsibilities**

**Operator Trials & Readiness**

* Own the operator work-trial program and ensure candidates are evaluated consistently.
* Maintain clear trial standards, evaluator guidance, and scoring criteria.
* Partner with recruiting and operations to continuously improve what the trial predicts about future operator success.

**New-Hire Onboarding**

* Build and run onboarding from day one through the first 30–60 days.
* Define what an operator should know and be able to do at each stage of ramp.
* Create training plans, checklists, certification steps, and readiness milestones.
* Identify struggling operators early and create clear paths for remediation.
* Continuously improve time-to-productivity for new hires.

**New Workflow Training**

* Partner with researchers and operations teams when new robot tasks, systems, or processes are introduced.
* Learn new workflows quickly and translate them into clear training materials and operating instructions.
* Design the rollout plan needed to train a large operator population quickly.
* Track who has been trained and verify that the training actually resulted in correct execution.
* Maintain consistency as training expands across shifts, teams, and locations.

**Training Operations**

* Maintain a clear training calendar and ensure training happens when required.
* Coordinate trainers, operators, shift leads, and researchers.
* Keep training materials current as workflows change.
* Build repeatable processes so training does not depend on tribal knowledge.
* Track training completion, readiness, and performance metrics.

**Continuous Improvement**

* Use operator performance data and feedback to identify gaps in training.
* Work with operations leaders to understand recurring quality or productivity issues.
* Determine whether problems are caused by training, instructions, process, tooling, or something else.
* Continuously simplify and improve how operators learn.

**What We're Looking For**

* Experience owning training, onboarding, or workforce development programs for hourly or frontline employees.
* Demonstrated ability to get new employees productive quickly.
* Experience building structured ramp programs with clear milestones and standards.
* Strong operational organization and follow-through.
* Able to turn ambiguous or technical workflows into simple, teachable processes.
* Comfortable managing trainers, who are responsible for training large groups of people on new procedures under tight timelines.
* Strong written and verbal communication.
* Able to work effectively with both highly technical stakeholders, trainers, and frontline operators.
* Comfortable in an environment where processes and requirements change frequently.
* Uses data and observation to improve training rather than relying only on subjective feedback.

Experience in robotics is not required.

*Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.*

jobs.title: Manager, Clinical Operations (CRAs)

jobs.title: IT Operations Manager, Infrastructure
jobs.description:
Citrin Cooperman offers a dynamic work environment, fostering professional growth and collaboration. We’re continuously seeking talented individuals who bring a problem-solving mindset, fresh perspectives, and sharp technical expertise. We know you have choices, so our team of collaborative, innovative professionals are ready to support your professional development. At Citrin Cooperman, we offer competitive compensation and benefits and most importantly, the flexibility to manage your personal and professional life to focus on what matters most to you!

We are looking for an experienced IT Infrastructure Operations Manager who also acts as the Delivery Manager for infrastructure projects. You will run the infrastructure intake process, track critical projects through to delivery, and provide timely, accurate metrics and status reporting to stakeholders. You will work closely with operations, engineering, vendors, and business teams so that infrastructure initiatives (migrations, upgrades, data center moves, new site rollouts) are well governed, visible, and delivered on schedule.

**Responsibilities are, but not limited to:**

* Design, document, and continuously refine the Infrastructure Projects Intake process, including request channels, intake forms and templates, triage and prioritization criteria, approval gates, SLAs, roles and responsibilities, and workflows (e.g., in ServiceNow, Jira, or Azure DevOps).
* Own and run the Infrastructure Intake process day to day, from request submission through triage, assessment, prioritization, and approval, working with architects, engineers, and security to validate scope, effort, dependencies, and risk.
* Maintain the intake queue and backlog, communicate decisions and timelines to requestors, and convert approved requests into projects with clear scope, owners, and milestones.
* Manage delivery of infrastructure projects from initiation through planning, execution, cutover, hypercare, and handover to operations, including cloud migrations, data center moves, server and storage refreshes, network and SD-WAN upgrades, DR implementation, and new site rollouts.
* Build and maintain project plans, schedules, RAID logs, and resource plans; apply the right methodology (Waterfall, Agile, or hybrid); run stage gates and project reviews; and manage scope changes through formal change control.
* Lead go-live readiness reviews and cutover planning, including operational acceptance criteria, test and rollback plans, change windows, and hypercare, so that new infrastructure is fully supportable before handover.
* Track all critical projects in a consolidated view, monitoring milestones, dependencies, and risks, and escalate slippage early with clear impact analysis and recommended actions.
* Maintain the infrastructure project portfolio and roadmap, forecast resource and capacity demand across teams and vendors, and align priorities with business needs, architecture standards, and the technology strategy.
* Define, collect, and publish delivery and operations metrics (project health, intake cycle times and backlog, on-time and on-budget rates, availability, MTTR, change success rate, patch compliance, vendor SLA performance) through dashboards and scorecards in Power BI, Tableau, Excel, or ServiceNow.
* Produce timely weekly, monthly, and quarterly status reports with RAG status, risks, issues, decisions needed, and upcoming milestones, plus executive summaries for steering committees and leadership reviews.
* Maintain stakeholder communication plans, RACI, and escalation paths, and coordinate business notifications and downtime approvals for planned changes and cutovers.
* Coordinate with operations teams so projects transition smoothly into support with runbooks, monitoring, and knowledge articles in place; participate in the Change Advisory Board (CAB); and follow ITIL-aligned incident, problem, change, release, and configuration processes, including CMDB accuracy.
* Track major incidents and problem records that affect projects or service levels, and follow root cause analysis (RCA) corrective actions through to closure.
* Coordinate with vendors, MSPs, cloud providers, and carriers on deliverables and timelines, and track and report on vendor performance against contracts and SLAs.
* Plan, schedule, and run Disaster Recovery (DR) tests, coordinating application owners, infrastructure teams, and vendors; document results, gaps, and remediation actions; and report DR readiness against RTO/RPO targets.
* Work with Information Security to ensure delivered infrastructure meets security standards, support audits and compliance requirements (ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, GDPR), and maintain risk registers.
* Track technology lifecycle and capacity, including end-of-life and end-of-support risk, license and contract renewals, and refresh planning, and feed the findings into the intake pipeline and roadmap.
* Close out projects with formal sign-off, post-implementation reviews, lessons learned, documentation handover, and benefits realization tracking.
* Track project and operational budgets, forecasts, and cloud costs (FinOps), and continuously improve intake, delivery, and reporting processes, promoting automation and Infrastructure as Code.

**The ideal candidate must:**

* Have a bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, engineering, or equivalent experience (required).
* ITIL 4 Foundation or higher; PMP, PRINCE2, or Agile/Scrum certification (PMI-ACP, CSM, SAFe) preferred.
* Having cloud certifications (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and ISO 27001 awareness are a plus.
* Have 8-12+ years in IT infrastructure, including experience running infrastructure projects and programs.
* Possess a proven track record managing and delivering medium to large infrastructure projects (migrations, data center moves, refreshes, network transformations).
* Have experience operating an intake or demand management process for infrastructure or IT requests.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Government
jobs.description:
For People is improving government digital services for the disadvantaged population. We work directly with government agencies to modernize software, systems, and platforms so that they better serve people.

**Your Impact**
---------------

Every month, hundreds of thousands of people go looking for facts about Medicare and Medicaid. They are researchers, reporters, policy staff, and health care providers. When the data is hard to find, a file is too large to post, or a column quietly changes its name between releases, their work slows down or goes wrong.

This project supports the website where the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) publishes that data for the public. It hosts a large catalog of datasets, lookup tools, and dashboards from across the agency, available for download, as interactive tools, and via a public API. As Program Manager, you will lead the team that builds and runs it. This is a hands-on role. You’ll facilitate partner meetings, support the team when they are blocked, and get into project details as needed to report clearly on the team’s progress. You’ll work elbow-to-elbow with the project’s technical and product leadership. You will learn about the work enough to identify and help mitigate delivery risks and hold the team accountable for what we promise to government partners.

This position is a full-time position **contingent** on For People being awarded a federal contract. If awarded, this position’s expected start date is February 2027.

**Our Culture**
---------------

For People is a team of humans. We place a significant amount of emphasis on positive work-life balance, setting healthy expectations, and making sure our loved ones are taken care of first. That means picking a child up from school during the day or going for a mid-day walk is okay!

This position is ***100% remote***. Our entire team is remote across the United States, from the West Coast to the East Coast. There will never be a return-to-office, as we have none! Occasional travel to CMS headquarters in Baltimore, MD (2-3 times per year) is required. These trips are infrequent and scheduled well in advance.

This full-time position's published base salary range is between **$100,000 and $160,000** annually. This band ranges across both the Program Manager and Senior Program Manager pay band, which will be determined based on relevant experience. All positions include generous benefits (e.g., For People pays 100% of Gold-tier employee health insurance premiums) and annual company profit sharing.

**Your Opportunities**
----------------------

On this project, you will be the delivery lead on a cross-functional team of about 15 people spanning engineering, design, user research, and support functions. The team may expand to up to 25 members in the future. As the Program Manager, you will:

* Build a collaborative and trusting team culture across all disciplines in the program
* Run agile practices including sprints, planning cycles, demos, and retrospectives, all of which include CMS stakeholders
* Coordinate with CMS offices that publish data on the public portal; share progress transparently and build positive working relationships with partner contracting teams
* Proactively identify and mitigate risks to project delivery
* Keep the program in line with contract, security, and accessibility requirements, including Section 508 and the site's Authority to Operate (ATO)
* Report status and outcomes to CMS and For People leadership, using live dashboards wherever possible and finding efficiency gains through automation
* Lead the handoff from the current contractor in your first few months so users see no disruption

**You Bring**
-------------

* A humble and caring attitude aligning with For People’s values: passion, fun, curiosity, sustainability, humility, and respect
* 8+ years of relevant experience in program or project management, including managing government contracts
* Degree in management, public administration, information technology, or a related field
* Experience with open data projects
* Experience managing cross-functional teams, with the ability to lead teams of 15 to 25 people as the contract grows
* Deep knowledge of agile product management principles
* Familiarity with collaboration tools such as Jira, Confluence, Slack, and GitHub
* Ability to oversee all aspects of task order management including reporting, sprint planning, and project planning
* Experience facilitating stakeholder engagement across multiple government agency offices and data owners

**It Would Be Great If You Also Have**
--------------------------------------

* Experience working directly with CMS programs or data
* Experience with public websites built on Drupal
* Experience leading a contract transition from an incumbent team

**Some Fine Print**
-------------------

You will be working on a United States government platform, and they have a few basic requirements for contractors like ourselves. All work must be physically performed within the United States at all times. In addition, you must be a United States citizen and be able to pass a government-performed public trust background check.  
  
For People is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, and/or veteran status.

**About UKON**

UKON exists to help every business survive a cyberattack.  
Formerly known as FifthWall Solutions, we have grown from our foundation as a specialized cyber insurance wholesaler into a full-service cyber revenue partner for independent insurance agencies and managed service providers. We give our partners the technology, processes, carrier access, and expertise they need to deliver sophisticated cyber capabilities without the cost and complexity of building an internal cyber department.  
Today, our team works inside our partners’ books of business to identify uninsured companies, understand their risk, secure the right coverage, and help get more businesses protected. With access to more than 50 carriers and differentiated coverage options, including custom endorsements for emerging risks such as agentic AI, we help businesses understand what they are buying and how their coverage will respond when they need it most.  
We are building the AI-native operating system that will make this work scalable. Our platform brings together fragmented agency data, cybersecurity context, carrier appetite, quoting, communications, and workflows to shorten the distance between an uninsured business and a protected one.  
For us, AI-native does not mean adding a chatbot to an existing product. It means embedding intelligence throughout the platform so the system can understand the context of a user’s work, recommend the right next action, and help complete that action within the workflow. Because we operate in insurance, we care as much about accuracy, reliability, auditability, data privacy, and user control as we do about model capability.  
Our mission is ambitious but simple: close the estimated $10 trillion cyber protection gap and ensure every business can survive a cyberattack.

**The Role**

You will be UKON's first Implementation Specialist, reporting to our executive team and working closely with our product, sales, and Cyber Practice Leaders (CPLs), teams. This is a greenfield role. You are being hired to build it.

UKON partners with independent insurance agencies and managed service providers to deliver an outsourced cyber practice. Signing a partnership is only the beginning. Implementation turns a signed agreement into an active, growing agency relationship: getting the agency onboarded, trained, connected to their CPL, and producing. Today that process runs on effort and goodwill. Your job is to turn it into a repeatable system.

You will design the agency onboarding standard, the handoff from sales to CPLs, the training standards, and the implementation playbook, and then run them. You will decide what good looks like, measure it, and keep improving it. This starts as an individual contributor role, with the opportunity to own and grow the implementation function as UKON scales.

Experience implementing technology and managing projects matters more to us than experience in insurance. If you’ve helped customers get up and running on a SaaS or technology product, kept projects on track, and built or improved the process along the way, we want to talk to you.

**What You'll Do**

* Build UKON's agency onboarding standard from the ground up, from signed agreement to active, producing partner.
* Design and run the handoff process between sales and Cyber Practice Leaders so nothing is lost between signature and launch.
* Create training standards and materials that get agencies and their producers confident and active quickly.
* Write and maintain the implementation playbook, including operating procedures, checklists, timelines, and escalation paths.
* Own the implementation pipeline for new agency partners and keep every account moving forward.
* Define implementation metrics, track progress, and report on what is working and what is not.
* Identify where agencies stall after signing and fix the root cause, whether it sits in process, product, or people.
* Partner with sales, CPLs, marketing, and product to feed agency feedback back into how we sell, support, and build.
* Use project management and AI tools to run implementation efficiently and at scale.

**What You Bring**

* At least 5 years of onboarding, implementation, or customer success experience with SaaS or technology products.
* A track record of building operating procedures and processes from scratch, not just following existing ones.
* Project management experience, including running multiple concurrent implementations with tools like Asana, Monday, ClickUp, or similar.
* Exceptional attention to detail and a process-driven, high-ownership approach to your work.
* The relational skill to work across sales, CPLs, and agency partners and earn their trust.
* Comfort coordinating and directing the work of others, even without formal authority.
* Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to turn messy processes into simple, usable documentation.
* Comfort operating in ambiguity and creating structure where none exists.

**Bonus Points**

* Experience in insurance, insurtech, or another regulated industry.
* Familiarity with independent insurance agencies, agency management systems, or managed service providers.
* Exposure to product management or experience feeding customer input into a product roadmap.
* Experience as an early hire who built an implementation or onboarding function.
* A property and casualty insurance license, or interest in obtaining one.

**What Success Looks Like**

* Every new agency partner follows a clear, documented path from signed agreement to active production.
* Sales and CPLs trust the handoff process, and agencies feel supported from day one.
* More signed agencies become active, producing partners, and they get there faster.
* UKON has an implementation playbook that can scale as we add partners and team members.
* Leadership has clear visibility into implementation progress and where agencies need help.

* Facilitate return-to-work efforts through coordination with employers and providers

**Administrative Functions**

* Maintain and update case review notes and documentation on all assigned cases

* Attend team meetings and training sessions as scheduled

* Strong organizational and time management abilities
* Attention to detail and accuracy in documentation
* Ability to work independently while recognizing when to seek supervision

* Basic analytical skills for routine case assessment
* Adaptability in a fast-paced work environment

**Education & Licensure:**

  

* High School Diploma required

**Experience:**

* 2+ years of clinical experience required
* Workers' compensation or disability management experience is highly preferred

**Skills:**

* Demonstrated organizational, technological, and communication skills
* Basic understanding of disability management principles
* Computer proficiency, including Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel), keyboard skills, and data entry capabilities

jobs.description:
Medical Editor – Arbitration & IDR Quality Assurance Specialist

**Elite Billing & Collections | Remote Position**

About the Position

Elite Billing & Collections is seeking an experienced, highly detail-oriented **Medical Editor** to join our growing Arbitration and Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) team.

This position is responsible for reviewing, editing, and strengthening arbitration submissions prepared by our paralegal team. The Medical Editor will serve as a critical quality assurance checkpoint, ensuring that every submission presents a clear, persuasive, medically accurate, and well-supported argument.

We are looking for someone who understands medical documentation, can identify weaknesses in written arguments, and has the ability to elevate the overall quality and effectiveness of our arbitration submissions.

Key Responsibilities

* Review and edit completed arbitration and IDR submissions prepared by paralegals.
* Evaluate the strength, clarity, accuracy, and persuasiveness of medical and reimbursement arguments.
* Strengthen medical narratives by highlighting procedural complexity, patient acuity, medical necessity, provider expertise, and other relevant clinical factors supported by the documentation.
* Review operative reports, clinical records, and supporting exhibits to ensure arguments accurately reflect the medical services performed.
* Identify weak arguments, missing information, inconsistencies, and opportunities to strengthen submissions.
* Ensure all claims and supporting statements are factually accurate and substantiated by medical records or other appropriate evidence.
* Verify medical terminology, procedural descriptions, diagnoses, and CPT codes for accuracy and consistency.
* Ensure submissions are professionally written, properly structured, and free of grammatical or formatting errors.
* Provide constructive feedback to paralegals to improve the overall quality of future submissions.
* Collaborate with paralegals and management to resolve documentation discrepancies and address quality concerns.
* Maintain high productivity and quality standards while reviewing a substantial volume of arbitration cases.
* Ensure submissions meet internal quality standards and applicable arbitration or IDR requirements.

Required Qualifications

* Professional experience in medical editing, medical writing, clinical documentation, medical billing, or a related healthcare field.
* Strong knowledge of medical terminology, anatomy, surgical procedures, and clinical documentation.
* Exceptional editing, proofreading, and professional writing skills.
* Ability to critically evaluate written arguments and identify opportunities for improvement.
* Experience interpreting operative reports and medical records.
* Strong attention to detail and ability to identify inconsistencies or unsupported statements.
* Excellent time management skills and ability to meet strict deadlines.
* Ability to work independently in a fast-paced, high-volume environment.

Preferred Qualifications

* Experience with medical arbitration, Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR), or the No Surprises Act (NSA).
* Experience reviewing medical necessity arguments, reimbursement appeals, or insurance disputes.
* Background in orthopedic surgery, spine surgery, pain management, or other surgical specialties.
* CPC, CCS, RN, or other relevant healthcare credentials.
* Experience in quality assurance, medical documentation auditing, or medical-legal editing.

What We're Looking For

**This is not simply a proofreading position.**

We need someone who can critically assess the quality of an arbitration submission, recognize where the medical or reimbursement arguments are weak, and make meaningful improvements that strengthen the case.

The ideal candidate will have exceptional analytical skills, strong medical knowledge, and the ability to ensure every submission is accurate, professional, persuasive, and supported by appropriate documentation.

Our goal is to produce consistently high-quality arbitration submissions that effectively communicate the medical complexity and relevant circumstances of each case.

How to Apply

Please submit your resume highlighting your experience in medical editing, clinical documentation review, medical writing, or healthcare reimbursement.

Candidates with experience reviewing complex medical records and strengthening medical or reimbursement arguments are strongly encouraged to apply.

Position is fully remote. Benefits not included except Paid Time Off.

Pay: $20.00 - $30.00 per hour

Benefits:

* Paid time off

Work Location: Remote

### **About MD Integrations**

At **MD Integrations**, we partner with digital health brands to power clinical care at scale. We specialize in men's and women’s health, dermatology, endocrinology, and weight management, offering telehealth solutions that help patients receive expert, personalized care—all from the comfort of their home. Join our team and be part of the movement to make specialty care more accessible and impactful.

**MD Integrations is an equal opportunity employer.** We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We are unable to support US visa sponsorship at this time.

We are looking for a mid-level Customer Success Manager to join our expanding team!

**Overview**

The Customer Success Manager (CSM) at MDI serves as the primary point of contact for our partners (customers) from kickoff through onboarding, go-live, and support as they grow. This role ensures partners experience a smooth, guided implementation of MDI’s telehealth infrastructure while building long-term, value-driven relationships.

This position reports to the Director, Partner Success, is remote (US) and full-time, generally Monday - Friday core hours. This partner-facing role must be comfortable on video and calls with partners, and shifting early or late to support partner onboarding and success.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead and project manage the full onboarding journey of new partners, from kick-off to go-live, ensuring clear milestones, proactive communication, and timely execution.
* Anticipate potential risks early, troubleshoot and escalate stalled or lagging partner progression by working closely with internal teams across CS, clinical, product and technical integrations teams. Serve as the guide and advocate for assigned partners.
* Act as the voice of the partner internally highlighting successes and opportunities with MDI’s service, platform and workflows. Collaborate with clinical and technical teams to provide feedback, relay product enhancements, and advocate for partner success.
* Increase partner health, engagement, and satisfaction, escalating issues as needed while continuously driving toward long-term retention and expansion. Track and report on key customer success metrics (NPS, csat, etc.) to executive and senior leadership.
* Provide ongoing support, education, and training to partners post-launch, with a focus on a seamless experience and optimizing integrations, workflows, and product adoption.
* Serve as a trusted advisor by providing market insights, best practices, and recommendations that align MDI’s solutions with partner growth goals.
* Manage and maintain consistent documentation on the customer lifecycle in internal systems, such as HubSpot, Asana, and other project and task management tools.
* Contribute to the development of key collateral, processes and defining standard expectations of work.

**Success in this role looks like**

* Partners achieve timely onboarding and confident go-lives with minimal friction. Communication is clear and consistent internally and externally.
* Partners feel consistently supported and guided through proactive, strategic communication through the post-sales cycle through onboarding and as they grow.
* MDI is positioned as a trusted advisor in helping partners scale their telehealth capabilities today and into the future.

**Qualifications**

* Experience by level:
* + **Associate-level** requires a minimum 1 year in Customer Onboarding, Customer Support, Customer Success or related customer-facing roles.
  + **Mid-level** requires a minimum 4 years in dedicated Customer Success or Account Management roles, preferably in a scale-up/fast-moving environment.
* Process- and project-oriented with a bias for action. Comfortable communicating clear deadlines, actions and risks with partners and internal leadership, driving toward aligned outcomes on behalf of the partner.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to build trust with business leaders, executives, clinical and technical customers and colleagues, navigate complex needs, and translate feedback to internal teams.
* Empathy for early-stage startup partners and an understanding of healthcare concepts. Able to quickly understand the challenges of building a brand from the ground up and advocate for partner needs internally.
* Proficient with CRM and general technology tools (e.g., HubSpot, Slack), and able to utilize metrics like NPS, churn, and activation to inform decision-making.
* Quick study with new concepts and terminology such as key healthcare terminology and workflows to support partners. Bonus points for experience in healthtech or telehealth, and comfortable with basic clinical terminology and concepts.

* **Competitive Salary:** The targeted range for Associate-level is $50,000 - $60,000 per year; the targeted range for Mid-level is $65,000 - $75,000 per year. The CSM also has regular opportunities to earn outcome-based bonuses aligned with partner productivity goals.
* **Comprehensive Benefits Package:** Our benefits package includes 75% subsidized health insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, paid time off, and a 401(k) retirement savings plan with company match.

65,000 - 75,000 USD per year(Remote (United States))

Dompé is an Italian bio-pharmaceutical company that focuses on innovation, where a long tradition in the field of personal wellness goes hand-in-hand with a commitment to research and development to meet unsatisfied therapeutic needs.

  

Established in 1940 in Milan, Dompé has an industrial and biotech research hub in L’Aquila, in addition to branches in Europe (Barcelona, Berlin, Paris and Tirana). The company has approximately 900 employees. The US headquarters of Dompé are based in Boston (R&D) and in the San Francisco Bay Area (Commercial Operations).

**YOUR ROLE AT DOMPÉ**

The Patient Access Manager reports to the Associate Director, Patient Access Manager and will be a key member of the US organization supporting the company’s efforts related to cenegermin eye drops, which are based on rhNGF (recombinant human nerve growth factor).

Approved in August 2018, OxervateTM eye drops (cenegermin-bkbj ophthalmic solution) is the first-ever topical biologic medication approved in ophthalmology and the first treatment indicated for neurotrophic keratitis (NK), a rare and progressive eye disease that can lead to corneal scarring and visual loss. Oxervate is also the first-ever application of a human nerve growth factor (NGF) as drug or treatment.

The Patient Access Manager (PAM) will be responsible for supporting and maintaining patient support services that maximize access to our product for patients to whom it has been prescribed. The PAM will execute pre-defined strategies and role requirements to address patient access needs. The PAM will manage specific service levels and contribute to managing the performance of the team. The PAM will also be a member of the field leadership team by playing a customer-facing role and work closely with our Field Access Managers (FAMs) to support the needs of physicians and their patients in the field (limited field travel as this role is primarily home office based). There is also an opportunity to collaborate with stakeholders across the company, influence the development of the Patient Services organization, and shape the culture of Dompé US.

The Patient Access Manager will be accountable for abiding by the core values of our Dompé culture, which are Integrity, Speed, Knowledge, Passion, Attention to Detail, Reliability, Flexibility and Teamwork. jobs.title: Patient Access Manager (Remote)
jobs.description:
**Overview**

Abax Health is a healthcare technology company dedicated to enhancing the patient's financial experience through data-driven engagement. Our platform and tech-enabled services enable hospitals and health systems to identify patients at financial risk, personalize outreach, and optimize patient access operations. By combining empathy with innovation, we empower providers to improve outcomes and drive operational performance.

**Mission & Vision**

Ensure that every patient receives the care they need, when they need it. To be the trusted source of patient access innovation increasing revenue and transforming patient access and financial clearance by reducing administrative burdens, uncovering untapped revenue, and improving the financial and clinical outcomes for patients and health systems across the United States.

**Location:** United States | Remote

**Location Eligibility:** Candidates must currently reside in the United States. This role is not available to residents of California, New Jersey, New York, Montana, Hawaii, or Alaska, or of any U.S. territory.

**Summary**

The Patient Access Manager leads Abax Health’s remote Patient Access operations across assigned client partners. Reporting to the Director of Patient Access Operations, this role leads supervisors who oversee patient registration, insurance verification, prior authorization, and scheduling teams. The Patient Access Manager is also the escalation point for performance, employee relations, and client concerns.

You will turn operational data into decisions. Supervisors handle day-to-day issues and produce reports. You analyze those reports to determine whether SLAs are being met, what is driving trends, and when to escalate to the client. You will use both spreadsheets and AI tools for this work, including building your own dashboards and agents.

This role suits an experienced Patient Access leader who is energized by a growing company. At Abax, managers partner closely with leadership during new client implementations and go-lives, then stabilize and grow the team after launch. You will support multiple clients and work alongside multiple leaders, and teamwork is central to how we operate.

**Responsibilities**

**Leadership and Team Development**

* Lead, coach, and develop Patient Access Supervisors and the teams they support.
* Set clear expectations for performance, accountability, and professional growth.
* Serve as the escalation point for corrective actions, performance improvement plans (PIPs), and terminations, in partnership with HR.
* Participate in interviewing and selecting Patient Access staff and supervisors.
* Build a team culture grounded in collaboration, ownership, and commitment to patient care.

**Patient Access Operations Oversight**

* Oversee team performance in patient registration, insurance verification, prior authorizations, and appointment scheduling.
* Ensure standardized workflows are carried out consistently across assigned client programs.
* Identify workflow inefficiencies and put scalable process improvements in place.
* Ensure compliance with HIPAA, client requirements, SLAs, and organizational policies.
* Ensure staff recognize when a conversation needs a qualified medical interpreter, such as clinical or consent discussions, and follow established interpreter and language access procedures.

**Performance Reporting and Analytics**

* Analyze supervisor-generated and system reports to evaluate SLA performance, productivity, quality, and work inventory.
* Identify upward and downward trends, determine root causes, and build action plans with supervisors.
* Escalate risks to clients proactively, such as work inventory shortages or performance gaps.
* Use Excel and AI tools, such as Claude, to build and maintain performance dashboards and reporting agents.
* Prepare clear, data-driven performance reporting for Abax leadership and client partners.

**Client Partnership and Implementation**

* Serve as a primary operational contact for assigned clients.
* Partner with leadership during new client implementations and go-lives, setting expectations with staff and clients before launch.
* Participate in client meetings, performance reviews, and issue resolution.
* Support onboarding of new clients, workflows, and technologies as Abax grows.

**Operational Excellence**

* Maintain process documentation and best practices.
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives that improve patient experience and operational outcomes.
* Adapt to changing client and payer requirements.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Bilingual Team Support (bilingual candidates only, not required)**

* Serve as a Spanish-language resource for supervisors and staff working bilingual lines.
* Support quality review of Spanish-language patient interactions.

**Qualifications and Experience**

**Required**

* High school diploma or GED.
* 3+ years of experience leading leaders, such as supervisors or team leads.
* 1+ year of direct supervisory experience in Patient Access.
* Experience overseeing teams that perform insurance verification, prior authorizations, and patient scheduling.
* Patient Access Manager experience or higher in a hospital, physician practice, healthcare call center, or similar patient-facing setting.
* Hands-on experience with electronic medical record (EMR) systems.
* Strong Excel and data analysis skills, with the ability to interpret reports and turn findings into action.
* Willingness to learn and use AI tools in daily work, including building dashboards and agents.
* Experience handling employee relations matters, including corrective action and performance improvement.
* Ability to work independently in a remote environment with limited day-to-day oversight.

**Preferred**

* College’s degree.
* Fluency in spoken and written Spanish and English. This is preferred, not required. Candidates who list Spanish fluency will complete a language proficiency assessment during the hiring

**Location** Work from Home **Job Category** Member Services, Geisinger Health Plan **Schedule** Days **Work Type** Full time **Department** GHP Medical Policy Division **Date posted** 10/15/2026 **Job ID** R-12313

### **Job Summary**

Supports overall efforts of the Medical Policy/Clinical Guidelines development area. Investigates and conducts audits of medical claims pursuant to changes in medical policy, and analysis of data to guide policy development and/or revision and makes recommendations to management. Conducts investigations and advises on the coverage status of claims based on current applicable medical policies, coding guidelines and industry information. Serves as a resource to assist staff with questions regarding medical policy implementation, coding, medical claims payment, claim edits and benefit set-up.

### **Job Duties**

  
  

Experience with **CPT coding, Medical Claims, Benefit Configuration** preferred

  
  

* Provides direction to benefits systems analysts to assure correct configuration of benefits by line of business and maintains the repositories for code configuration changes as a result of medical policy development and government directives.
* Conducts research and retrospective review of medical claims in an attempt to determine and ensure compliance with contractual, state and federal regulations.
* Completes requests for and reviews of medical records to validate services billed to the medical benefit with unlisted or miscellaneous codes.
* Research reimbursement, medical record documentation, utilization and proper coding.
* Reviews clinical documentation to determine eligibility of coverage.
* Makes recommendations to system set up for proper claims adjudication with regard to benefit coverage.
* Develops and maintains databases to catalog code status as related to medical policy, and state or federal mandates.
* Maintains and manages coding matrix and databases associated with contracted vendors, prior authorization requirements, Preventive Services, non-covered services and Experimental and Investigational or Unproven services.
* Makes presentations to various committees regarding the configuration of benefits and claims to support medical policy development initiatives.
* Produces ad hoc reporting to determine pre- and post-implementation utilization trends
* Identifies operational deficiencies and areas where process improvement would decrease the company's exposure with regard to medical claims payment as it relates to benefits, coverage and financial liability.
* Investigates and conducts audits of medical claims, analyzes data, to guide policy development and revision and reporting capability.
* Conducts review and coordinates multi-departmental implementation of annual new codes, quarterly updates and assigns new coding to treatment types which assures appropriate cost-sharing tiers.
* Continually audits claims and ensures compliance with current coding guidelines and industry information utilizing Health Plan policies.
* Addresses claims payment errors as revealed through claims audit and retrospective review.
* Process claims in Facets workflow that pend for medical policy implementation specialist manual review.
* Reviews claim research request forms (CRRF) for claim adjustment determination.
* Acts as resource for CPT/HCPCS code advisement to various GHP workgroups ad hoc.
* Participates in standing GHP operational meetings as needed.
  

  
  

Work is typically performed in an office environment. Accountable for satisfying all job specific obligations and complying with all organization policies and procedures. High School Diploma or Equivalent (GED)- (Required)

Minimum of 2 years-Relevant experience\* (Required)

Communication; Leadership; Health Care Policy And Ethics Compliance

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, pregnancy, genetic information, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected category under applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Everything we do is about making better health easier for our patients, our members, our students, our Geisinger family and our communities.

jobs.title: Stars Population Health Measure Optimization Lead
jobs.description:
**Become a part of our caring community**
=========================================

The Stars Population Health Business Intelligence Lead will help the team move from reporting activity to generating actionable intelligence. Success in this role will be reflected in stronger population visibility, clearer performance accountability, faster identification of improvement opportunities, more rigorous evaluation of initiatives, and better-informed decisions that support Stars performance and member health outcomes.

**Description**

Health Quality and Stars (HQS) is responsible for improving health outcomes and advancing the care experience of members and provider partners through quality solutions. HQS is committed to caring for customers and delivering high plan quality as rated by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS).

The CMS Stars quality rating system evaluates Medicare Advantage and Prescription Drug Plans across measures that include preventive care screenings, health condition management, health outcomes, patient experience, and plan operations.

The Stars Population Health Business Intelligence Lead will provide advanced analytics, population insights, and reporting capabilities that enable the Stars Population Health Strategy team to improve performance among priority populations. The role will translate complex data into a clear understanding of performance drivers, member needs, program effectiveness, and opportunities for action across unpaneled members, new members, multi-gap members, and the Annual Preventive Visit enterprise strategy.

This role will partner across Stars and the enterprise to strengthen data availability, define meaningful performance measures, monitor outcomes, and create decision-ready insights. The role requires both deep technical expertise and strong business judgment, with the ability to influence stakeholders, establish shared accountability, and connect analytics directly to population-specific strategy and execution.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Analyze member-level Stars, demographic, engagement, program, and operational data to identify performance drivers, emerging trends, and opportunities within priority populations.
* Develop code, reports, dashboards, and repeatable analytical capabilities that support population strategy, initiative performance monitoring, and executive decision-making.
* Create clear data visualizations, executive summaries, and strategic narratives for immediate colleagues, enterprise partners, and senior leadership.
* Collate and manipulate data from multiple sources, including Oracle, SQL, Excel, and enterprise reporting environments, while documenting available data, dependencies, quality considerations, and gaps.
* Build population definitions, segmentation approaches, baselines, targets, and measurement frameworks for unpaneled members, new members, Pragmatic Planner segments, multi-gap members, and Annual Preventive Visit performance.
* Conduct Stars performance and demographic analyses across relevant perspectives such as geography, contract, product, measure, member segment, intervention, and channel.
* Own deep, holistic operational reporting for priority initiatives and provide regular executive-level rollups that clarify performance, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions.
* Measure initiative effectiveness and member outcomes, identify what is and is not working, and recommend strategy adjustments based on evidence.
* Monitor performance of critical populations within existing programs and assess how outreach and engagement efforts can be better coordinated to reduce unnecessary touchpoints and improve effectiveness.
* Use forecasting, scenario analysis, and predictive techniques, where appropriate, to estimate opportunity, prioritize focus areas, and support resource allocation decisions.
* Become a subject matter expert in member-level Stars measure specifications and the underlying data used to identify performance drivers and improvement opportunities.
* Partner with strategy, clinical, operations, technology, member-facing, provider-facing, and analytics teams to improve data accessibility and embed population insights into enterprise tools and routines.
* Provide independent, data-supported recommendations and influence cross-functional partners to create shared accountability for Stars Population Health priorities and results.
* Support the design and evaluation of targeted, longitudinal strategies for hard-to-reach populations, balancing optimization of existing programs with selective innovation.

**Key Competencies**

* Advanced analytical thinking and data interpretation
* Business intelligence and data visualization
* Population segmentation and opportunity sizing
* Performance measurement and outcomes evaluation
* Strategic storytelling and executive communication
* Cross-functional influence and relationship management
* Independent judgment and strategic decision-making
* Prioritization and execution in a fast-moving environment

**Use your skills to make an impact**

We provide secure, efficient, and tailored services to financial institutions and businesses, enabling seamless transactions for their customers. new_jobs.description:
Job Description:

**Business Operations Manager**

**CIRCE Technology & Research, Business Development**

**Agency Overview**

Felton Institute responds to the needs of our community by providing innovative, evidence-informed social services that transform lives. Our organization offers 60+ programs that address mental health, the unhoused, early care and education, those impacted by the justice system, transitional age youth, as well as aging adults. Our programs combine the latest scientific research with cultural sensitivity and a deep commitment to supporting and reflecting the communities we serve. Felton offers a dynamic, challenging, and supportive work environment where we encourage the use of professional development, that staff can utilize throughout their career.

**Program Description**

CIRCE Technology & Research is a Salesforce consulting and product firm serving nonprofit, behavioral health, and human services organizations. CIRCE is a registered Salesforce ISV Partner and Consulting Partner and has been in the Salesforce partner program since 2011. CIRCE is a wholly owned subsidiary of Felton Institute.

CIRCE serves the Felton Institute along with sixteen external community-based organizational clients across five service lines: Salesforce consulting and development including Agentforce, systems migrations, the CIRCE Software App for Care and Case Management, Crisis Response Solutions for 988 contact centers and mobile crisis dispatch, and Managed IT Services.

**Position Summary**

We are seeking a Business Operations Manager to keep CIRCE's client relationships, projects, billing, and internal operations running on a consistent, documented footing. This role sits in Business Development and works across the full client lifecycle, from prospect research and demonstrations through contracting, project tracking, invoicing, training, and ongoing account support.

The central purpose of this role is continuity. You will document how CIRCE's business operations run, serve as backup to the Director of Business Development, and build systems that do not depend on any one person's knowledge.

This is a generalist role. The right candidate is organized, follows a process through to completion, is comfortable working inside Salesforce, and can move between client-facing work, financial administration, and research in the same week.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Customer Success and Client Support**

* Train client staff on CIRCE products and their Salesforce environments.
* Support account management, including client check-ins, issue follow-up, and coordination with the delivery team.
* Assist with live product demonstrations for clients and prospects, including at conferences.

**Project Operations**

* Maintain CIRCE's project portfolio in Monday.com, including status updates, timelines, and Gantt charts for active projects.
* Enforce CIRCE's project procedures so that no work begins until required documentation is in place, including:  
  + Master Services Agreement (MSA)
  + Statement of Work (SOW) and Engagement Plan
  + Invoicing terms
  + Project start date, milestones, and deadlines
  + Written estimates for additional client requests before work begins
* Track client licenses, renewal dates, and license counts.
* Maintain an accurate, current client list.

**Salesforce Administration and Reporting**

* Enter and maintain client and prospect information in CIRCE's internal Salesforce org.
* Clean up and deduplicate records to keep data reliable.
* Build reports and dashboards for internal use and for clients.
* Complete entry-level Salesforce configuration and support tasks on behalf of the delivery team.

**Billing and Financial Operations**

* Assist with monthly client invoicing and annual license invoicing.
* Support the Stripe integration with Harvest and its ongoing use for billing.
* Help design and maintain a client numbering system.
* File processed invoices digitally in CIRCE's designated document system.
* Support financial and compliance audits by locating and preparing documentation.

**Business Development and Research**

* Research prospects and competitors ahead of meetings and prepare concise meeting briefs.
* Identify and research private, corporate, and federal funding opportunities, including eligibility screening, and recommend which to pursue.
* Assist in creating presentations for leadership meetings, including the Leadership Roundtable, and for client and prospect audiences.

**Marketing and Digital Presence**

* Review website and LinkedIn analytics monthly, identify patterns, and recommend actions to strengthen the CIRCE brand.
* Draft social media posts and route them for approval and publication.
* Obtain client testimonials and case study material.
* Monitor and manage CIRCE's shared email inbox.
* Maintain CIRCE's online booking page.
* Assist with conference and event planning, logistics, and follow-up.

**Hiring Support**

* Work with Felton Human Resources to develop and update job descriptions.
* Post open positions on recruitment sites such as LinkedIn
* Enter job requisitions in iCIMS and monitor each hiring process through to close.

Department Overview
  
  
Welcome to Electric Asset Strategy (EAS). We are responsible for asset strategy, standards, procedures, and end-to-end risk management for 2.3 million structures across the electric distribution system. We deliver risk-informed strategic plans that leverage inspection insights and asset data to guide maintenance and investment decisions.
  
  
The Distribution Asset Risk Management (ARM) team—comprising Asset Failure Analysis (AFA), Asset Insights, and Inspections & Maintenance Strategy (I&M)—focuses on continuously improving how PG&E monitors and maintains its assets to support a resilient, reliable grid and help keep our communities safe.
  
  
Position Summary
  
  
The Program Manager, Expert will lead the development, implementation, and financial stewardship of I&M strategy programs for PG&E’s electric distribution assets. The role will translate regulatory requirements, asset condition insights, risk analysis, budget planning, accounting considerations, and operational constraints into executable multiyear strategies and work plans that improve safety, reliability, compliance, affordability, and risk-spend efficiency.
  
  
This position requires strong accounting, financial analysis, investment planning, and practical AI literacy to develop defensible budgets, forecasts, business cases, and funding recommendations. The successful candidate will apply sound judgment, protect confidential information, validate outputs against authoritative sources, and maintain clear human accountability. The role will establish performance measures, monitor program and financial results, challenge assumptions, and present clear recommendations to senior leaders and governance forums.
  
  
The Program Manager, Expert will also provide critical regulatory support and may serve as a General Rate Case (GRC) witness assistant, helping coordinate the development of accurate, consistent, and well-supported testimony, workpapers, exhibits, and discovery responses. The role will lead cross-functional responses to regulatory data requests—often on short notice—by rapidly organizing subject-matter experts, validating operational and financial data, documenting assumptions and source support, identifying risks and inconsistencies, and delivering high-quality responses within firm deadlines. Strong partnerships across Asset Strategy, Inspections, Maintenance, Operations, Engineering, Wildfire Risk, Regulatory, Compliance, Finance, Accounting, Law, Technology, data teams, vendors, and external partners will be essential to meeting program and regulatory commitments.

new_jobs.title: Medical Editor – Arbitration & IDR Quality Assurance Specialist
new_jobs.description:
Medical Editor – Arbitration & IDR Quality Assurance Specialist

**Elite Billing & Collections | Remote Position**

About the Position

Elite Billing & Collections is seeking an experienced, highly detail-oriented **Medical Editor** to join our growing Arbitration and Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) team.

This position is responsible for reviewing, editing, and strengthening arbitration submissions prepared by our paralegal team. The Medical Editor will serve as a critical quality assurance checkpoint, ensuring that every submission presents a clear, persuasive, medically accurate, and well-supported argument.

We are looking for someone who understands medical documentation, can identify weaknesses in written arguments, and has the ability to elevate the overall quality and effectiveness of our arbitration submissions.

Key Responsibilities

* Review and edit completed arbitration and IDR submissions prepared by paralegals.
* Evaluate the strength, clarity, accuracy, and persuasiveness of medical and reimbursement arguments.
* Strengthen medical narratives by highlighting procedural complexity, patient acuity, medical necessity, provider expertise, and other relevant clinical factors supported by the documentation.
* Review operative reports, clinical records, and supporting exhibits to ensure arguments accurately reflect the medical services performed.
* Identify weak arguments, missing information, inconsistencies, and opportunities to strengthen submissions.
* Ensure all claims and supporting statements are factually accurate and substantiated by medical records or other appropriate evidence.
* Verify medical terminology, procedural descriptions, diagnoses, and CPT codes for accuracy and consistency.
* Ensure submissions are professionally written, properly structured, and free of grammatical or formatting errors.
* Provide constructive feedback to paralegals to improve the overall quality of future submissions.
* Collaborate with paralegals and management to resolve documentation discrepancies and address quality concerns.
* Maintain high productivity and quality standards while reviewing a substantial volume of arbitration cases.
* Ensure submissions meet internal quality standards and applicable arbitration or IDR requirements.

Required Qualifications

* Professional experience in medical editing, medical writing, clinical documentation, medical billing, or a related healthcare field.
* Strong knowledge of medical terminology, anatomy, surgical procedures, and clinical documentation.
* Exceptional editing, proofreading, and professional writing skills.
* Ability to critically evaluate written arguments and identify opportunities for improvement.
* Experience interpreting operative reports and medical records.
* Strong attention to detail and ability to identify inconsistencies or unsupported statements.
* Excellent time management skills and ability to meet strict deadlines.
* Ability to work independently in a fast-paced, high-volume environment.

Preferred Qualifications

* Experience with medical arbitration, Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR), or the No Surprises Act (NSA).
* Experience reviewing medical necessity arguments, reimbursement appeals, or insurance disputes.
* Background in orthopedic surgery, spine surgery, pain management, or other surgical specialties.
* CPC, CCS, RN, or other relevant healthcare credentials.
* Experience in quality assurance, medical documentation auditing, or medical-legal editing.

What We're Looking For

**This is not simply a proofreading position.**

We need someone who can critically assess the quality of an arbitration submission, recognize where the medical or reimbursement arguments are weak, and make meaningful improvements that strengthen the case.

The ideal candidate will have exceptional analytical skills, strong medical knowledge, and the ability to ensure every submission is accurate, professional, persuasive, and supported by appropriate documentation.

Our goal is to produce consistently high-quality arbitration submissions that effectively communicate the medical complexity and relevant circumstances of each case.

How to Apply

Please submit your resume highlighting your experience in medical editing, clinical documentation review, medical writing, or healthcare reimbursement.

Candidates with experience reviewing complex medical records and strengthening medical or reimbursement arguments are strongly encouraged to apply.

Position is fully remote. Benefits not included except Paid Time Off.

Pay: $20.00 - $30.00 per hour

Benefits:

* Paid time off

Work Location: Remote

**Company:** Avail Health

**About Avail Health**

Avail Health is a Nurse Practitioner-founded, rapidly growing healthcare organization dedicated to improving access to high-quality care for Medicare-age individuals. Through innovative, technology-enabled virtual and mobile care models, we support patients with complex medical, behavioral health, and social needs.

Our team is passionate about improving patient outcomes, empowering clinicians, and building scalable care delivery solutions for underserved senior populations.

**About the Role**

Avail Health is seeking an experienced **Coding & Risk Adjustment Specialist** to support our growing clinical programs in a flexible, part-time consulting capacity.

In this role, you will serve as a subject-matter expert in Medicare Advantage risk adjustment, HCC coding, and clinical documentation integrity. You will collaborate closely with clinical and operational leadership to strengthen coding accuracy, optimize documentation practices, conduct audits, and develop scalable workflows that support compliance and program performance.

* Experience reviewing clinical documentation and advising healthcare providers on coding accuracy and documentation best practices.

* Proficiency with electronic medical record (EMR) systems, coding tools, and documentation review processes.

**Preferred Qualifications**

new_jobs.description:
Dompé is an Italian bio-pharmaceutical company that focuses on innovation, where a long tradition in the field of personal wellness goes hand-in-hand with a commitment to research and development to meet unsatisfied therapeutic needs.

  

Established in 1940 in Milan, Dompé has an industrial and biotech research hub in L’Aquila, in addition to branches in Europe (Barcelona, Berlin, Paris and Tirana). The company has approximately 900 employees. The US headquarters of Dompé are based in Boston (R&D) and in the San Francisco Bay Area (Commercial Operations).

**YOUR ROLE AT DOMPÉ**

The Patient Access Manager reports to the Associate Director, Patient Access Manager and will be a key member of the US organization supporting the company’s efforts related to cenegermin eye drops, which are based on rhNGF (recombinant human nerve growth factor).

Approved in August 2018, OxervateTM eye drops (cenegermin-bkbj ophthalmic solution) is the first-ever topical biologic medication approved in ophthalmology and the first treatment indicated for neurotrophic keratitis (NK), a rare and progressive eye disease that can lead to corneal scarring and visual loss. Oxervate is also the first-ever application of a human nerve growth factor (NGF) as drug or treatment.

The Patient Access Manager (PAM) will be responsible for supporting and maintaining patient support services that maximize access to our product for patients to whom it has been prescribed. The PAM will execute pre-defined strategies and role requirements to address patient access needs. The PAM will manage specific service levels and contribute to managing the performance of the team. The PAM will also be a member of the field leadership team by playing a customer-facing role and work closely with our Field Access Managers (FAMs) to support the needs of physicians and their patients in the field (limited field travel as this role is primarily home office based). The PAM will work with the team to improve existing materials as well as identify, design, and roll out patient access materials as needed. There is also an opportunity to collaborate with stakeholders across the company, influence the development of the Patient Services organization, and shape the culture of Dompé US.

The Patient Access Manager will be accountable for abiding by the core values of our Dompé culture, which are Integrity, Speed, Knowledge, Passion, Attention to Detail, Reliability, Flexibility and Teamwork. Individuals must possess an entrepreneurial spirit, be flexible, and adaptable to new situations.

**WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING:**

The Patient Access Manager (PAM) plays a critical, non-promotional role focused on facilitating patient access to Oxervate through advanced case management support. PAMs are responsible for handling escalations from external vendors and serve as key coordinators in the patient care journey. By closely collaborating with Field Access Managers (FAMs), vendors, and Eye Care Physicians (ECPs), they ensure patients receive the necessary support throughout the access process. Once patient services are initiated, PAMs work within compliance guidelines to address and resolve any access barriers that may arise.

Serve as the key point of contact for FAMs regarding patient access questions or concerns.

* Reimbursement Process Oversight: Monitor the end-to-end reimbursement process by partnering with the hub vendor and Specialty Pharmacy to triage and resolve issues such as prior authorizations (PAs), denials, appeals, reauthorizations, overrides, and billing discrepancies.
* Provider Communication & Education: Engage with healthcare providers to educate on the Dompé Connect to Care program, answering questions as appropriate to keep the patient journey on track
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with Market Access, National Access Managers (NAMs) and FAMs to ensure accurate and timely updates on insurance approvals and reauthorizations for patients enrolled in the Oxervate Patient Journey.
